newsitem.title: USA: Maine Gov proposes $3.77 bln FY 1998-1999 budget.
newsitem.headline: Maine Gov proposes $3.77 bln FY 1998-1999 budget.

text.p: Maine Gov. Angus King Tuesday proposed a $3.77 billion budget for the 1998-1999 fiscal years that would defer a cap on income tax collections that is scheduled to take effect next year.
King said his budget will close a projected $360 million shortfall without imposing new taxes, and includes $142 million "in real cuts" - such as the elimination of the state's liquor store system.
"We make painful cuts but the most important things is that it establishes an unmistakable downward trend in the overall bite that taxes take out of the pockets of Maine people," King told reporters.
King complained that Maine's taxes were curbing the state's economic growth because they are 20 percent higher than the national average.

The proposal has spending growth of about 4 percent, but much of that money is destined to replace revenues lost from a hospital tax whose scheduled elimination could cost the state an additional $540 in matching federal funds.

King projected that deferring the the income tax cap for at least two years should save the state $130 million in lost revenue. The Legislature approved the cap last year without identifying potential spending cuts.
King said "discretionary growth" in the budget include more money for the Corrections Department, which has seen a sharp growth in its prison population because of new laws limiting early release.

The budget would increase general purpose state aid to education by 1 percent in 1998 and 2 percent in 1999. King proposed a similar increase to the University of Maine system contingent on the system cutting administrative costs by 2 percent.

King said is budget curbed spending growth by refusing to automatically give departments inflation-related budget increases. The proposal has $12 million in inflation-related growth compared to $59 million in the 1996-1997 budget, he said.
